subject: Civil Engineering
title: The Itaipu Dam
description: Learn The Itaipu Dam in one minute.

hook.text: Itaipu generates more electricity annually than any other dam — powering Paraguay and Brazil.

buildup.text: Straddling the Paraná River border — a joint project between two nations, built 1975-1984.

discovery.text: 14,000 MW capacity — Itaipu supplies 75% of Paraguay's electricity and 15% of Brazil's.

twist.text: The construction diverted a river and removed 50 million tons of earth — reshaping geography.

climax.text: The dam produced a record 103 billion kWh in 2016 — equivalent to powering 50 million homes.

punchline.text: Two nations, one river, shared power. Itaipu proved that engineering can unite countries.

quiz.question: What makes Itaipu Dam unique among the world's largest dams?
options: It's the tallest dam ever built by any country
It generates more electricity annually than any other single hydropower plant
It was constructed entirely underwater without diverting the river

details.summary: Itaipu Dam on the Parana River between Brazil and Paraguay was the world's largest hydroelectric dam by annual energy output for decades, generating over 100 billion kilowatt-hours in peak years. Its 196-meter-high hollow gravity dam combines concrete and rock-fill sections across a 7.
details.whyItMatters: Itaipu supplies about 90% of Paraguay's electricity and 15% of Brazil's, demonstrating how a single dam can power an entire nation and transform a regional economy.
takeaways: It produces more cumulative energy annually than any other hydroelectric dam
The dam combines different structural types to span a very wide valley
International cooperation between Brazil and Paraguay enabled the project

faq.question: How does Itaipu compare to Three Gorges in power generation?
faq.answer: Three Gorges has higher installed capacity at 22,500 MW versus Itaipu's 14,000 MW. However, Itaipu's more consistent water supply allows higher utilization, and it has produced more cumulative energy in many years.

faq.question: Why does the Itaipu dam use multiple structural types?
faq.answer: The Parana River valley at the dam site is 7.7 kilometers wide with varying geological conditions. The project uses a concrete gravity section at the river channel, a hollow gravity section for the powerhouse, and rock-fill embankment sections across the floodplain.
